bio: Backend engineer. I write about Django, distributed systems, and the boring parts that keep products alive.
about:
I've spent the last seven years building backends for fintech and developer tools — mostly Python, mostly Django, occasionally Go when latency matters.

My writing here is a running notebook: things I had to learn the hard way, benchmarks I wish someone had published, and the architectural trade-offs nobody puts in the README.

Outside work I maintain a couple of small open-source libraries and answer far too many questions about database indexes.

bio: Product designer working on design systems and the unglamorous craft of consistency.
about:
I design systems, not screens. Most of my day is spent negotiating between what a component should do and what six different teams have already made it do.

I write about tokens, documentation, and why the hardest part of a design system is the social contract around it.

bio: Full stack developer. TypeScript, Postgres, and an unreasonable number of side projects.
about:
Full stack by necessity rather than ideology. I like the part of the job where you can see the whole path from a click to a row in a table.

Here I mostly publish walkthroughs — the kind I'd want to find at 1am when something is on fire.

bio: Engineering manager. Thinking out loud about teams, systems, and the space between them.
about:
I manage two platform teams and spend most of my time on the interfaces between people rather than services.

I write about hiring, on-call culture, and how technical decisions quietly become organisational ones.

bio: ML engineer. Retrieval, evaluation, and being suspicious of benchmarks.
Writing about developer experience, docs, and the tools that get out of your way.
about: Technical writer turned DX engineer. I believe most onboarding problems are really documentation problems wearing a costume.
